about: Where the TF2 Voice Emulator stands. Read CLAUDE.md first, then this. The orchestrating session keeps this file; builders do not edit it.

stands.live: https://neb882.github.io/source-VOIP-converter7/ serves main (GitHub Pages from the branch root).
stands.model: The Steam profile from microphone to sound device, the voice gate and the receiver are read and measured (tests/REFERENCE_2026.md). vaudio_celt and vaudio_celt_high run the game's own CELT 0.11 build and reproduce its recordings to all but 1 and 75 samples in 292,000, each one step off. The speex profile runs the game's Speex 1.0.2 as its module does; against a real recording it is equal within one unit in 63% of frames and the same sound, coded differently, in the rest. The rooms are a module confirmed against recordings and not yet in the render (W3-17c, being built).
stands.last_merged: W4-01a with W4-01c (2026-11-11, cache v34): the page's journey and its access. A chosen or dropped file, a recording or a demo's speaker renders by itself and the player comes into view with the focus (nothing plays by itself); a changed setting renders again 0.4 s after the last change on a source of at most a minute and keeps the place in the clip, and on a longer one marks the result as made with earlier settings; a render that was cancelled or that failed is not started again by itself; presets light when the controls match them, a line under them says what differs from the defaults, with Reset; settings are remembered in the browser (settings and saved presets only; a share link wins); 'Render' for 'Process Audio', 'Hear: Rendered | Original' for the wet/dry button; a status line under the player with the codec in the menu's own words; the version in the footer and a notice when a newer one is ready. Access: Tab leaves the console, a refused microphone gets a plain sentence, larger controls on a phone, the console's feed no longer read out, meters and the picture described. No audio file touched and no hash moved; the browser suite goes from 299 to 374 checks. Review: one blocking fault (a failed render restarted itself twice a second) and four test gaps, all fixed, each with a check shown to fail. docs/reports/W4-01ac-page.md. Before it: BC-1 (2026-11-11, cache v33): on Steam voice a lost packet is a whole sender message. Loss is drawn once per message (Packets lost %, labelled net_fakeloss); a lost message's frames are encoded and not decoded; when the next message of the phrase arrives Steam's decoder conceals up to 10 of the missed frames and any more time stays silent, later sound keeping its place; a packet coming to more than 12 frames with its concealment is refused whole; a lost end marker leaves the decoder as it was for the next phrase; the live chain equals the render under loss. Five steam hashes moved, no other. The other profiles keep the per-frame bursts of about 2.2 frames. Private check against Set C: the build equals the planner's prototype sample for sample; accuracy level column loss15 -1.4 dB before, +0.0 after; combined -1.7, +0.3; loss5 +0.1, +0.4; speech_loss10 +0.2 before, +0.4/+0.5 after (0.3 dB further from 0, cause unknown). The builder's placement of a played packet replaced the order's formula (the prototype was wrong under heavy jitter). Review: no defect; five test gaps closed, each test shown to fail with its piece disabled; two flaws of the frame log (no sample changes) recorded in the report. At the merge the orchestrator made the page's 'Frames per packet' sentence say that Steam voice ignores it. docs/reports/BC-1-loss-per-message.md. Before it: W3-20b (2026-11-11, cache v32): the Miles voice codec as a profile, `miles`, labelled as not in TF2 everywhere it shows. As the Source engines of 2006 and 2007 ran it: 11025 Hz in and out with no resampling, 360-sample frames of 32.65 ms and 12 bytes, 2940 bit/s, the wrapper and VR12 codec of W3-20a, the receiver's gain on the decoder's samples, a delay of 305 samples (the median of a measured grid; it moves by up to 15 samples with the grid). The codec control has two groups, 'Team Fortress 2' and 'Not in Team Fortress 2' (Fullband Opus and vaudio_miles); a note shown, and read to screen readers, only while Miles is chosen says it is not a TF2 codec and has not been checked against any recording of a running engine; a render's status line says 'Voxware VR12 (not in TF2)'. Stand-ins, said as such in the docs: both codec objects reset at a new spurt, the gain held across spurts, a lost frame as 360 zeros with no decoder call. No accuracy row, no registered prediction. No hash of another profile moved. Review: nothing blocking; three sentences and one accessibility fault fixed. docs/reports/W3-20b-miles-profile.md. Before it: W3-17d with W4-01d (2026-11-11, cache v31): rooms on the page and in the live chain, and a help sentence under every setting. A room control (none by default, the named rooms, a dsp_room number, under water) for renders and for the live chain; the live chain keeps one room path per session and attaches or lets it go at 512-sample block starts, so that letting go and attaching again changes no sample against a path left attached (shown at 11025, 22050 and 44100 Hz); the 11.6 ms hold is counted in the latency only while held. Two reviews: the first found one blocking item (the live room's test compared the module with itself) and five lesser ones, the second a one-sample tick at release and re-attach and a stale flag in the worker; all fixed, each with a check that fails on the code before it. No recorded hash moved; no private run was owed. docs/reports/W3-17d-rooms-page.md, docs/reports/W4-01d-settings-words.md. Before it: W3-19 (2026-11-11, cache v30): the engine codecs' receiver gain on the decoder's own samples. For celt_22, celt_44 and speex the gain runs on the decoder's stream from its first sample (the codec's delay of 64, 128 and 80 samples kept in front) and the delay is dropped after it, in process() and createRender(); the live chain and a demo's voice already did. Privately (the orchestrator, the whole render at voice_maxgain 10 on the game's own captured input): Set M 145,966 of 145,966 samples (before: 86,171); Set H 158,384 of 158,548 samples that are not silence (before: 45,123), the rest one known sample a step off and 163 in the recording's last packet. Reviewed: an independent reference equal in 648 of 648 cases and 54 of 54 with re-timing, the live chain's gain equal to the render's; no major finding, two minor ones fixed. Nine recorded renders moved (the three profiles with the gain on); nothing at voice_maxgain 1, with the gain off, or of another profile. Before it: W3-18 (2026-11-11, cache v29): Speex 1.0.2 with the arithmetic of the game's module. The build patches 25 places in 7 files of libspeex (tests/speex102/patch.mjs) and has the module's float cosine and arc cosine written afresh from a specification in words (tests/speex102/vsx_math.c, SPEC-cosf-acosf.md, tables generated by gen-tables.mjs). Equal to the module run in a CPU emulator on seven clips (147 of 147 frames), on 21,389 and 22,155 arguments of the two routines, and on the tests' five runs. Privately (the orchestrator, on the build): Set M's gain-1 recording in 145,920 of 145,920 samples, the gain-10 recording in 146,080 of 146,080 after the app's gain on the whole decoded stream. Reviewed: a byte-identical rebuild from fresh clones, the two routines equal natively and in WebAssembly on all 2^32 arguments, 11 of 11 output-changing mutations caught, no major finding, three minor ones fixed. Only Speex hashes moved. Before it: W3-17c (2026-11-11, cache v28): the engine's rooms in the render. A room or under water renders through room-dsp.js after W3-10's entry (the voice entered twice at its direct and room shares, each upsampled on its own, the tail ended by the module's rule, cap 20 s); createRender streams a room (outputLength, maxTail); the old room code and the listener's low-pass are gone; five ROOM_PLACES rows for ctf_2fort. No hash of a render without a room moved. Reviewed (an independent model equal on 11,582,872 of 11,582,872 samples; six small findings fixed). Privately: every no-room take unchanged in every figure; Set C with set_c_room +1.2 to 0.0 dB against the take and its echoes equal (0.2363 against 0.2335 at 57.96 ms); Set D PC A one echo of three 36% high, unexplained. The page still offers the old choices, mapped onto the new rooms; the room panel and the live chain are W3-17d. Then W3-20a (2026-11-11): the Miles codec module, with no change to the page or the cache.
stands.ci: The tests workflow runs on every push and can be started by hand. Until 2026-11-09 one browser check (the live recording's lag) failed by chance about once in thirty runs; W1-04 removed the cause, so a red run is a real failure. A branch made before W1-04 still has the old check until it merges main. On 2026-11-11 from 13:56 UTC every run stopped before any test: Ubuntu's package mirrors could not be reached from the runners while Playwright fetched extra fonts. Since 5a8ca56 the workflow installs the browser from Playwright's servers first and gives the system packages three minutes; if the mirrors do not answer the suite runs on the runner image's own libraries and says so in a warning. A missing library would fail the browser suite at launch, not pass it.
stands.takes: Since 2026-11-09 the owner's takes are in a private repository a session can attach (the owner knows its name; it is not named here). It holds Sets A to F as FLAC, the Set D demo, the source speech and clip, and the three test signals as played; the checksums of the Set D and F files match tests/REFERENCE_2026.md. The two songs played for Set A are there too. Not found: take1_default.flac (only the voice_maxgain 10 take of that pair; the tests accept either). stands.baseline: 2026-11-09, main at 61fcb92: tests/accuracy.mjs on the 16 takes of Sets B to F gives every figure of the 'Every take' table in tests/REFERENCE_2026.md to the last digit shown, so the review fixes, the demo reader and Speex moved nothing in the measured model. The Set D demo answered W1-02's open question: Steam's sequence numbers restart at 0 after each end marker (REFERENCE finding 11). Set A and tests/retiming.mjs reproduce the document too. Read block by block (2026-11-09, a scratch copy that kept each half-second block): on the owner's speech 231 of 246 blocks are within 0.5 dB and 239 agree to 0.18 dB rms; the 7 others are the quiet half-seconds where a talk spurt ends (take -48 to -52 dBFS, the game's ambience in the recording against the model's silence) or where the receiver moved a spurt. On the test signal 170 of 177 agree to 0.20 dB rms and the 7 others are the known cases of findings 13 and 14. So the accuracy table's 0.96 and 1.45 dB are those few blocks, not a general error. What is left on the modern preset for speech is when phrases start: the game started 9 of this take's spurts 100 to 340 ms early or late, which the render models only as an option (voice_retime, findings 19 and 21).
stands.priority: The owner cares most about the modern preset (the Steam profile at defaults), which they have A/B tested against the game. Work on it comes before the legacy codecs and the rooms.
stands.console: The game's 'find voice' output (2026-11-09, kept in the private repository) gives the receiver's defaults: voice_buffer_ms 100, voice_fadeouttime 0.1, voice_overdrive 2, voice_overdrivefadetime 0.4, voice_steal 2, voice_avggain 0.5, voice_maxgain 10, voice_scale 1. Its help for sv_voicecodec calls vaudio_celt '22kHz, 22kbps' and vaudio_celt_high '44kHz, 44kbps', which the celt_44 profile (256-sample frames, 120-byte packets) does not match: W3-03 checks it. The debug variables exist in this build: voice_recordtofile (writes voice_micdata.wav and voice_decompressed.wav), voice_inputfromfile (reads voice_input.wav; sv_allow_voice_from_file defaults to 1), voice_writevoices, voice_showincoming, voice_showchannels, voice_profile.
stands.phrase_timing: W3-01 (2026-11-10, from the takes alone): the receiver's queue model beats the flat 41% rule on held-out takes (speech and the Set C baseline: -9.7 against -20.0 log-likelihood over 21 transitions; the flat rule cannot chain early starts and the speech take has two chains), with L0 350 ms, a 62.5 ms silence record and a ceiling at L0. Its limits: from the source alone it reproduces 41% of speech transitions (flat rule 31%), never the whole pattern, and on 6 of 8 takes moving spurts places them worse than leaving them, because the game's pauses on speech come out about 50 ms longer than the gate model predicts. New, and in neither model: a restarted spurt plays 25 to 50 ms late and the receiver skips that much audio within half a second, on 13 of 14 restarts seen. Three constants are fitted, not understood; W3-03 reads the engine for the rule.
stands.debug_run: 2026-11-10, the owner's first run of the game's debug variables (kept in the private repository as Set G; a first reading by the orchestrator, to be checked against the engine by W3-03). With voice_showincoming and voice_showchannels the console prints every packet added to the voice channel and the channel's queued bytes on every frame. Read from it: packets are 60 ms (three frames) and a spurt's first is 160 ms; the queue never exceeds 0.5 s (22050 samples at 44.1 kHz) and 103 of 1,520 packets landed on that limit, so what did not fit was dropped (about 25 ms each); after a spurt's first packet on an empty channel the queue does not drain for 25 to 30 frames whatever arrived meanwhile (about 340 to 410 ms: the restart latency is a time, not a fill level); the mixer takes 512-sample blocks. voice_inputfromfile does nothing under the Steam codec (the owner heard only the microphone), and voice_recordtofile wrote only 5 to 8 s: no sample-exact tap of the Steam path that way. Third run (frame-rate test, 2026-11-10): the owner's fps_max is 300, and with fps_max 67, 100 and 300 the wait before a channel plays was 7, 11 and 31 ticks, against the 6 to 7, 9 to 10 and 30 the engine's rule predicts; the queue at the start was 220, 288 and 500 ms, and packets overflowed the ring only at 300 (14 of them). So the frame-rate dependence is confirmed by experiment. SourceTV did not run on the local server (no demo), so the decoder cannot be checked sample for sample from this run; its voice_decompressed.wav with the gain at 1 is the decoder's own output for one key press.
stands.receiver: W3-03 (2026-11-10, docs/reports/W3-03-engine-binary.md): the receiver's queue was read from the owner's engine file and agrees with the owner's console log (Set G) on every count checked. A voice channel is a 0.5 s ring at 44.1 kHz; overflow drops the oldest sound, heard as a skip. A packet for a speaker with no channel opens one, resets the gain to 1.0 and starts a countdown of voice_buffer_ms (100) that falls by one FRAME's duration per 15 ms TICK, so the wait before playing is about 100 ms at 67 fps, 345 ms at 233 fps and 450 ms at 300 fps, and what is queued at the start is at most 0.5 s less the 160 ms a spurt opens with: about 350 ms on a fast PC, which is the L0 the takes gave. A spurt whose first packet arrives before the ring is found empty is appended (W3-01's rule, plus a grace of one tick); otherwise the channel is freed and the next packet restarts. One sample is dropped from every packet, which is the 400 ppm every take runs fast by (not a recorder's clock). The last voice_fadeouttime (0.1 s) of a queue is faded. The gain law of findings 3 and 4 is confirmed, with small corrections: the ramp divides by 127, the block mean is an integer, a decoded block of zeros sends the gain to its cap, and the gain resets when a channel is assigned. Not found in the voice path: the [0.1, 0.8, 0.1] output stage. Legacy codecs: vaudio_celt is 22050 Hz, 512 samples, 64 bytes at complexity 5 (the app runs 10); vaudio_celt_high is 1024-sample frames in 128-byte packets fed 22050 Hz sound (the app's celt_44 runs a table row the engine never selects); the engine asks vaudio_speex for quality 3 at 11025 Hz. voice_inputfromfile is not read under the Steam codec but is under vaudio_celt (22050 Hz, 16-bit mono, beside the executable); voice_recordtofile writes up to 11.9 s per key press, after the gain.
stands.gain_exact: 2026-11-10, Set H (the owner ran vaudio_celt with a known file as the microphone, voice_maxgain 1 and then 10, voice_recordtofile on): the engine's gain rule as W3-03 read it, applied to the gain-1 recording, gives the gain-10 recording sample for sample over 291,840 samples (570 packets; only the last packet differs, and that differs between the two key presses). The integer block mean and the rule that a decoded block of zeros sends the gain to its cap are both needed for that (2,798 and 234 of the 291,840 samples differ without them; 3,309 and 745 counted over the whole file with its last packet); the divisor 127 or 128 makes no difference on this signal. The app's present rule differs on 3,032 samples. This is the first sample-exact check of any receiver stage against the game, and the gain code is shared with the Steam path. The same set shows vaudio_celt in 512-sample packets and vaudio_celt_high in 1024-sample packets, both at 22050 Hz. The app's CELT did not match it (17.7 dB); W3-08 found why. Since W3-05 (2026-11-10) the app's own gain code gives the same 0 of 291,840, and a second read of the gain function found every float operation single precision and separate, the per-sample product a 32-bit multiply that wraps, and the reset writing unity for the first block with the settings read only then.
stands.celt_exact: W3-08 (2026-11-10, docs/reports/W3-08-celt-encoder.md): the game's CELT is the source the app already pins, built with its pitch pre-filter and post-filter compiled in (the app's build has them out). With that build switch, a reset after creation, 16-bit entry points with ties to even, and the two-sample start of the engine's file reader, the project's own WebAssembly build gives Set H's vaudio_celt recording at 292,351 of 292,352 samples and its vaudio_celt_high recording at 292,789 of 292,864, the rest one step off (the orchestrator re-ran the check). vaudio_celt_high is the 44100 Hz mode with 1024-sample frames and 128-byte packets, run on 22050 Hz sound. The bundled decoder refuses any real vaudio_celt packet whose filter flag is set, so a demo's CELT voice does not decode today where the voice is pitched. Built and merged as W3-06 (2026-11-10): the app's own module now gives those figures, and Set I's recording at 145,919 of 145,920.
stands.mixer_output: W3-07 (2026-11-10, docs/reports/W3-07-mixer-output.md), read from the owner's engine.dll and checked against Sets B and D: the mixer runs at a fixed 44100 Hz in 512-sample blocks; a voice channel is copied in sample for sample (no rate conversion, no interpolation, no spatialisation, no filter) at 255/256 truncated toward zero; the sum of voice and game sound is clipped at +-32767, then multiplied by volume and rounded. voice_overdrive never touches the voice itself. The roll-off above 12 kHz that the model fits with the 3-tap [0.1, 0.8, 0.1] is not in the game: it is the system mixer's linear interpolation from 44100 to the device's 48000 Hz (flat tops stay exactly on the ceiling; a 1 kHz tone has images at 2900 and 4900 Hz at -64 to -67 dB in five recordings, predicted -65.4 and -66.2; response sinc squared, equal to the 3-tap within 0.1 dB up to 13 kHz and 1.1 dB lower at 18 kHz). On a 44100 Hz device there would be no roll-off (inferred, no take). Listener B is explained: volume 0.11 (ceiling 3604 = round(32767 x 0.11)) and voice_scale 0.77 on that PC, which with the engine's gain rule gives its staircase; REFERENCE's 'about 0.077' and finding 15's reading of B are wrong. Not modelled and not needed for the takes: the room and water DSP a voice also passes through. Since W3-10 (2026-11-11) the app runs all of it as read, in exact integers: the entry at 255/256 truncated, the engine codecs' upsampling by two, the clip, volume and rounding with ties to even, then the device stage (linear interpolation to the listener's device rate, 48000 Hz by default, none at 44100). The 3-tap filter, the float volume, the output's sinc resampler and the soft limiter are gone; a render is at the device's rate; volume's default is 1. On the owner's takes the model minus the recording at 12 to 16 kHz went from -0.76 and -1.00 dB to -0.03 and +0.04 (music) and from -1.84 to -0.06 (speech): the fitted filter had no images, the interpolation and the recordings have them. The device stage against a lossless retake (2026-11-11): the linear rule and ties to even after volume confirmed; as built equal in 49% and within one unit in 73% of samples, within one unit in 98.2% with the read position drifting as a single-precision one would (2^-25 mix sample per output sample) and 99.5% with the voice 0.0011 sample late; a one-unit loss toward zero in about a quarter of samples is unexplained. Inaudible; a read of the XAudio2 module would be for equality to the unit only.
stands.steam_sender: W3-09 (2026-11-10, docs/reports/W3-09-steam-voice.md), read from the owner's steamclient64.dll and checked against Set G's logs and Set D's demo. Capture at 24000 Hz in steps of 750 samples; each Steam frame (about 55.85 ms) takes the whole steps captured since the last as one chunk; the gate is open when the chunk's mean of |x| is at least 1.0% of full scale or its peak at least 15%; an opening sends the last 100 ms (2400 samples) before the chunk with it; the hold is 0.4 s of wall-clock time; key up is followed by 0.5 s more capture; one chunk is one message; frames of 480 are cut from kept plus chunk; the end marker resets the encoder and the sequence number. Encoder: libopus 1.1.4, VOIP, 32 kbit/s, DTX on, complexity default 9 (the project's build gives the same packets at 8 to 10), 16-bit entry points. Decoder: concealment capped at 10 frames; the 24 to 44.1 kHz step is libswresample at its defaults, called once per packet with a flush, which gives the logs' sample counts exactly (7056, 2646, 882). Not yet tested by the owner: Steam's console variables mic_inputfile (a file in place of the microphone under the Steam codec) and @voice_spew_activity_check; clips for that run are in the private repository.
stands.speex_module: W3-09 section 5, read from a vaudio_speex module the owner supplied (32-bit, from HL2DM): Speex 1.0.2 (float), narrowband, the engine's quality 3 mapped to Speex quality 4, 160-sample frames in 20 bytes, constant bit rate, no VAD or DTX, enhancement on, complexity default. The module does not resample: 11025 Hz sound goes into the 8 kHz codec as it is, so a frame is 14.51 ms, the real rate 11.025 kbit/s and the band reaches 5.5 kHz; decoded floats are truncated to 16 bits with no clamp. The app's speex profile (1.2.1 with resampling to 8000 Hz) is to be rebuilt accordingly (W3-12). No recording of Speex can be made from a current game: asked for vaudio_speex, the engine starts vaudio_celt (Set I, a third recording the corrected CELT build reproduces, 145,919 of 145,920 samples; the fall-back was then found in TF2's engine.dll, W3-09 section 6). Corrected 2026-11-11 (Set M): a recording of Speex can be made. HL2DM's launcher starts the 64-bit game, which cannot load the 32-bit module; started with -force32bit the game runs vaudio_speex (packets of 160 samples at 11025 Hz). The app's Speex on the game's own captured input equals the game's decoded recording within one unit for the first 2.35 s and in 575 of 912 frames; in the rest it is the same sound at the same level (0.014 dB apart, the difference 13 dB under), coded differently from one frame on and equal again after quiet stretches: most likely the two builds' float arithmetic in the encoder's search (not established). Only the gain-1 recording was scored. Settled 2026-11-11 by an investigation (the module read, then run in a CPU emulator, where it equals the game's recording in 145,920 of 145,920 samples and executes no x87 instruction): its arithmetic is SSE2 compiled with the fast floating-point model, 25 places in 7 files of libspeex 1.0.2 differing from strict C (sums eight at a time, three double expressions in float, two reciprocal multiplies, re-ordered additions, four float library calls). A patched plain-C prototype equals Set M's gain-1 recording in 145,920 of 145,920 and the gain-10 one after the app's gain in 146,080 of 146,080, natively and as WebAssembly, and equals the emulated module on 255,746 synthetic frames provided the float cosine and arc cosine are the C runtime's own (not correctly rounded); with stand-ins it parts from the module about once in 250,000 frames. No dependence on the processor found. To be built: W3-18. Since W3-18 (2026-11-11, v29) the app's build has that arithmetic and equals Set M's decoded stream in every sample at both gains (the orchestrator's private run on the build). The whole render at voice_maxgain 10 equals it too since W3-19 (v30). Measured by the owner 2026-11-11 in TF2 itself (build 11191711 started with -force32bit, sv_voicecodec vaudio_speex confirmed by the console, voice_loopback 1, voice_showincoming 1): 226 voice packets, 191 of 320 samples and 35 of 480, all multiples of Speex's 160 and none of CELT's 512, and no "Unable to load" line. So TF2's 32-bit game runs vaudio_speex; the fall-back to vaudio_celt is the 64-bit game's. The docs were corrected at W3-19's merge. Set O (2026-11-11, private): the owner's recordings of Speex in TF2's own 32-bit game, Set M's method and input, at voice_maxgain 1 and 10. The app at v30: the bundled codec in 912 of 912 frames; the whole render in 145,966 of 145,966 samples at both gains. TF2's gain-10 recording is the same file as HL2DM's, the gain-1 ones equal over Set M's length. So the speex profile is checked against current TF2 itself, end to end up to the gain.
stands.sender_demo: 2026-11-10, a private run of steam-sender.js (W3-02b) against what Steam sent in Set D's demo (20 spurts, 1,816 messages, 5,109 frames; the scripts are in the private repository). With the demo's own chunk lengths as the clock and the demo's decoded sound as the microphone: spurt starts within one chunk (62.5 ms) in 18 of 20 and ends within two chunks in 18 of 20 (W3-11a's bars: 17 and 16); the four misses are the decoded sound differing from the microphone's (a -36 dB pink step and a 20 Hz sweep that decode under the gate, tones above 11.5 kHz that decode to almost nothing). With the test signal itself as the microphone: 16 spurts message for message the demo's, the 727-, 429- and 924-frame ones among them, starts 20 of 20, ends 19 of 20. Not falsified: the frame cutting and one chunk per message; the pre-roll (2400 samples in 18 openings, 1500 after a record, 0 from the ended state); the silence record one chunk long and absent when the next chunk is active; pauses of 20 to 200 ms bridged and 500 ms not; a hold of 0.4 s from the read of the last active chunk (bounded to 375 to 406 ms). Known bias, in the DRAWN clock and not in the rule: with seeds 1 to 200 the 440 ms pause between spurts 19 and 20 is bridged in 194 seeds where Steam split it, because the drawn clock ends a spurt on the 8th chunk about 94% of the time where the demo has the 7th in half; the model's tails after the loud part average 482 ms against Steam's 462 in this demo (the old 22-frame gate: 444). The owner's planned Steam console run with @voice_spew_activity_check prints each chunk's length and verdict and is the data to refit the clock on. Also: the decoded sound is 156 samples (6.5 ms) late against what the gate saw; and the demo's voice ticks are multiples of 4 (60 ms).
stands.steam_exact: W3-14 (2026-11-10, docs/reports/W3-14-steam-file-input.md), the owner's Steam console run with a file in place of the microphone (Set J, private). The app's parts, driven by Steam's own chunk lengths, give Steam's recording of the continuous clip in 524,286 of 524,288 samples (11.889 s) under the fma3 kernel; the two others are one step off and come from one decoded sample that lies one float step from a rounding boundary. The other kernels differ in 59 to 108 more. Settings of the match: libopus 1.1.5, 24000 Hz, VOIP, 32000 bit/s, DTX on, VBR, complexity 9, the 16-bit decode, one message per chunk, one resampler per decoder with the first-packet flush. All 789 gate verdicts follow the rule (mean at least 1.0% of 32767, or a sample at least 4915); all 645 lines of the game's log are reproduced; the pre-roll matches sample for sample. New: the hold is 0.4 s on a 32-bit float clock whose step depends on how long that clock has run (1/8 s in this run, where all 12 spurt ends fall four steps after the last active read; 1/32 s fits Set D), which explains the sender's bias toward the 8th chunk; Steam reads every 48 to 64 ms, nearly uniform, never late; a key press resets the encoder and the kept samples, not the sequence number or the gate's state; the decoder and resampler outlive key presses.
